column3: {{refn|After [[World War 1]] Poland received a small part of historical [[Lower Silesia]], with majority [[Poles|ethnic Polish]] population as of year 1918. That area included parts of counties [[Syców]] (German: Polnisch Wartenberg), [[Namysłów]], [[Góra]] and [[Milicz]]. In total around 526 square kilometers with around 30 thousand inhabitants, including the city of [[Rychtal]]. Too small to form its own voivodeship, the area was incorporated to [[Poznań Voivodeship (1921–1939)|Poznań Voivodeship]] (former [[Province of Posen]]).|group=Note}}
column6: {{refn|Interwar Silesian Voivodeship was formed from Prussian [[East Upper Silesia]] (area 3,225 km<sup>2</sup>) and Polish part of Austrian [[Cieszyn Silesia]] (1,010 km<sup>2</sup>), in total 4,235 km<sup>2</sup>. After the annexation of [[Zaolzie]] from Czechoslovakia in 1938, it increased to 5,122 km<sup>2</sup>. Silesian Voivodeship's capital was [[Katowice]].|group=Note}}
